title: Greedy Sidon construction size lower bound

problemStatement.formal: theorem greedySidon_size_lower_bound (N : ℕ) (hN : N ≥ 1) : size (greedySidon N) ≥ Nat.sqrt N
problemStatement.plain: Prove that the greedy Sidon construction in {1,...,N} produces a set of size at least √N (or c√N for some explicit constant c > 0). This was previously stated as an axiom in Erdos156Problem.lean and subsequently removed. Formalizing the proof would close the gap.
whyMatters: Establishes a concrete lower bound on the greedy construction, complementing the maximality proof
The key counting argument (at step k, at most k² sums can block) is a standard technique worth formalizing
Combined with the Erdős-Turán upper bound, pins down the greedy Sidon set size to Θ(√N)

knownResults.goal: Prove the size lower bound |greedySidon(N)| ≥ c√N

currentState.focus: Initial creation as follow-up from erdos-156 completion
currentState.nextAction: Formalize the counting argument: at each step, the number of blocked elements grows quadratically in |A|

knowledge.progressSummary: BLOCKED: Problem statement incorrect. The greedy Sidon set in {1,...,N} has size Θ(N^{1/3}), not ≥√N. For large N, N^{1/3} < √N, so the claim is false. The correct lower bound is cN^{1/3} for some constant c.
insights: At size k, the greedy set blocks ~k^2 new elements, so total blocked after k additions is ~k^3/3
Greedy terminates when k^3/3 ≥ N, giving size ≈ (3N)^{1/3}
For N=10000: greedy size ≈ 17, but √N = 100. The √N bound is FALSE
nextSteps: Correct formal statement to: size (greedySidon N) ≥ c * Nat.iroot 3 N for some constant c
The Θ(N^{1/3}) bound is the correct result for the greedy Sidon construction
